correctness.rationale: Every position in a minimal output belongs to either chosen embedding, giving multiplicity at most two. A unique zero forces C0C. With two zeros, any uniquely occurring nonzero symbol j forces the left factor to be 0,1,...,j-1 and the right factor to be j+1,...,n-1,0, hence 0C0. All other cases have two copies of each symbol and length 2n. The explicit paired word (1,0)(2,1)...(n-1,n-2)(0,n-1) has unique disjoint input embeddings for all n>=3. Finite alignment enumeration checks n=2..8; direct Cartesian enumeration independently checks n=2..4. Neither finite check substitutes for the proof.

value.rationale: The one-step rotation of a permutation is a canonical test of minimal versus shortest merging. A minimal output can be almost twice as long as the shortest one, but its length cannot take n-3 consecutive intermediate values. More strongly, every below-maximum minimal output is one of two explicit rigid words. This is a complete infinite structural classification, not a routine small numeric increment or checker-only assertion; it exposes a sharp forbidden-length phenomenon relevant to minimal-supersequence enumeration and output-length variation.
